answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity’s action timing, resource use, and interaction graph are hashed per epoch; a re-registration must match its prior fingerprint within a tolerance band, or the identity starts at zero reputation and cannot forge trust history. To survive, an attacker must operate every sock puppet across many epochs, mimicking stable organic drift—an orchard of dormant accounts diverging naturally. The cost is sustained compute, storage, and coordination latency per identity, plus near-total loss of any synthetic history that skips a mesa of quiet epochs.
